callout.title: Recommendation
callout.body: Sign-ready after three redlines to §8.2 and the liability cap. The economics are fine; the renewal mechanics are the only real exposure.
points: Redline §8.2: notice 90 → 30 days; consider deleting auto-renew entirely.
Raise the liability cap from 1× to 12× annual fees (data processor).
Either way, calendar the Nov 30 2027 notice deadline now.
callout.footer: Want me to draft the redline markup and a one-paragraph cover note to their counsel?

verdictcard.title: The call
verdictcard.label: Ship it, carefully
verdictcard.verdict: Build the search rewrite first, behind a flag, and gate the quarter on its p95.
verdictcard.reason: Four of five headline features ride on the new index, derisk it before anything leans on it.
verdictcard.caveat: If the index migration slips two weeks, cut Polish from Q3, not the search hardening.
verdictcard.footer: The roadmap below holds either way, this only changes what ships last.

companionnote.reflection: Four weeks of short nights is a lot to carry — no wonder the days feel heavier.
companionnote.follow: The numbers aren't a verdict on you; they're just showing what your body's been asking for.

positioncard.title: How worried should you be tonight?

levels.label: Usually fine
levels.detail: Alert between spikes, drinking, wetting diapers — a fever the body is handling.

levels.label: Watch closely
levels.detail: Clingy and drained but still responsive; recheck in a few hours.

levels.label: Call tonight
levels.detail: Hard to rouse, breathing fast, or under 3 months with any fever.

positioncard.reason: A playful-between-spikes, drinking child sits at the reassuring end — how they look matters more than the number.
watchFor: A stiff neck, a rash that does not fade under a glass, or trouble breathing
No wet diaper in 8 hours, or no tears when crying
positioncard.caveat: This places the situation, it does not diagnose it — your read of your child wins.

differential.title: What is usually behind a fever like this

causes.name: A common viral infection
causes.tell: Runny nose or cough, comes and goes over a few days
causes.pointsAway: A fever lasting past day 5 with no other symptoms

causes.name: Ear or throat infection
causes.tell: Tugging at an ear, pain swallowing, or fussier lying down
causes.pointsAway: No ear or throat complaints at all

causes.name: A urinary infection
causes.tell: Fever with no cold symptoms, especially in younger kids
causes.pointsAway: An obvious cold already explaining it

causes.name: A serious bacterial infection
causes.tell: Very drowsy, stiff neck, or a non-fading rash

differential.prompt: Look for the tell-tale signs above — a cough or runny nose usually points to the common, harmless causes.
differential.caveat: These are possibilities with honest odds, not a diagnosis; a clinician can examine and confirm.

reframecard.title: A gentler take
reframecard.thought: I bombed that interview, so I am clearly not cut out for this role.
reframecard.reframe: One hard interview is a single data point, not a verdict on your whole career — you answered three of the five questions well, and that is something to build on.
reframecard.footer: Notice the jump from one moment to a whole identity — that is the part worth questioning.

breathpacer.title: A moment before bed
breathpacer.note: A slow 4-7-8 breath nudges your body toward rest — try a few rounds as the lights go down.

copingmenu.title: When Wednesday feels like too much
copingmenu.intro: Pick whatever feels possible — you don’t have to do all of them.

options.label: Take three slow breaths before the next call
options.detail: Resets your shoulders so the back-to-back stretch starts a little calmer.

options.label: Decline or shorten the one meeting that could move
options.detail: Even reclaiming 20 minutes makes the crunch breathable.

options.label: Step outside for a short walk at lunch
options.detail: A change of light and air between blocks, no agenda.

options.label: Block the first hour tomorrow as protected focus
options.detail: Gives the rest of the week one place that stays yours.

copingmenu.footer: None of these have to be perfect — one is plenty for a heavy day.

subtextdecode.title: What your sister might mean
subtextdecode.message: Fine, do whatever works for you. I'll figure out my own ride.

readings.interpretation: She is hurt and hoping you will offer to drive her after all
readings.cue: “Fine” plus “I’ll figure out my own ride” often signals disappointment, not agreement

readings.interpretation: She genuinely has another plan and is letting you off the hook
readings.cue: “whatever works for you” can be a sincere release with no edge to it

readings.interpretation: She is annoyed and pulling back from the conversation
readings.cue: the clipped, short reply could read as withdrawing rather than wounded

subtextdecode.cantKnow: Tone does not travel well over text, so you cannot be sure which of these it is from the words alone.
subtextdecode.reply: Hey, that message felt a little off to me — are you actually okay with the plan, or would you rather I drove you?

rehearsal.title: Rehearsing the chat about taking the car keys
rehearsal.opener: Dad, I love you and I want you safe — can we talk honestly about the driving?

branches.reaction: get defensive or insist they are fine
branches.say: I hear you, and this isn’t about taking anything away — it’s about keeping you on the road as long as we safely can.
branches.why: Names the fear behind the resistance and keeps you on the same side.

branches.say: We don’t have to settle it now. Could we just try one daytime drive together this week and see how it feels?
branches.why: A small, time-boxed step is far easier to agree to than a verdict.

branches.reaction: ask what the alternatives even are
branches.say: Good question — I’ve looked at the senior shuttle and splitting rides, so you’d keep your independence.
branches.why: Shows you came with options, not just a problem.

rehearsal.exit: Let’s sit with it and revisit on Sunday — no decision today.
rehearsal.footer: Lead with care, give him a small next step, and let him keep his dignity.

messagescriptset.title: What to say to cancel the three you forgot
messagescriptset.intro: Each one has its own quirks, so the wording differs. Copy the line, send it, and keep the rebuttal handy.

scripts.message: Please cancel my subscription effective at the end of the current billing period. I do not want it to auto-renew. Can you confirm the cancellation in writing?
scripts.rebuttal: If they offer a discount to stay: "Thanks, but I’d still like to cancel today and reconsider later if I need it."

scripts.message: I’d like to cancel my membership. Please tell me the exact notice period and the final charge date so there are no surprises, and confirm once it is processed.
scripts.rebuttal: If they cite a long notice window: "Please send me the clause that requires it, and start the cancellation clock from today."

scripts.message: I’m calling to cancel my plan and turn off auto-renewal. Since I just renewed, am I within the refund window, and what do I need to do to qualify?
scripts.rebuttal: If they say no refund: "Can you note my account that I asked to cancel today, in case the window is calculated from a different date?"

messagescriptset.footer: Cancelling all three frees up about $41/month toward your December goal.

talktrack.title: How to open the resignation call

lines.say: Thanks for making time, I wanted to tell you this directly rather than over email.
lines.note: Sets the tone before the news lands.

lines.say: I have decided to move on, and my last day will be two weeks from today.
lines.note: Say the date plainly, then stop talking.

lines.say: This was a hard call. I have learned a lot here and I am grateful for it.
I want the handover to go smoothly, so let us plan the next two weeks together.

talktrack.footer: Let the silences sit. You do not owe a full explanation, only a clear decision and a clean exit.

faq.title: Questions the team keeps asking

items.q: Why re-platform instead of patching v2?
items.a: Three services with diverging schemas made every search change a three-way migration. One typed core makes the next two years of features cheap, the rewrite pays for itself by Q4.

items.q: What happens if the backfill slips again?
items.a: The flag stays at 0% and we ship the command bar against the <mark>legacy</mark> index as a fallback. GA moves a week; nothing else in the plan breaks.

items.q: Can partners stay on the old SDK?
items.a: Yes, the v2 SDK is supported through the end of next quarter. A codemod migrates 90% of call sites automatically.

items.q: How do we roll back during cutover?
items.a: The flag flips read traffic back to legacy in seconds. We keep legacy reads warm until W11 specifically so rollback stays free.

faq.footer: If your question is not here, drop it in #atlas-v3 and we will add it.

tabs.label: Scope
tabs.body: In: typed core, new search index, command bar, saved views, instant filters. Out: theming, export v2, and the mobile shell, all explicitly deferred to v3.1.

tabs.label: Rollout

accordion.title: The rollout plan, section by section

sections.label: Phase 1, Typed core behind a flag
sections.body: Stand up the single typed search core, dark-shipped at 0% traffic. Every read still hits the legacy index; the new path runs in shadow so we compare results query-for-query before a single user sees it.

sections.label: Phase 2, Backfill & shadow reads
sections.body: Backfill the historical index and ramp shadow reads to 100%. The gate to advance is a <mark>p95 within 5%</mark> of legacy across all query types, long-tail included.

sections.label: Phase 3, Cutover to GA
sections.body: Flip read traffic over in steps (5 → 25 → 100%), keeping legacy reads warm the whole time so rollback stays a one-second flag flip. GA when the new core has owned 100% of reads cleanly for a week.

accordion.footer: Each phase is independently reversible, the flag is the safety net at every step.

promptset.title: A gentle close to the day

prompts.question: What is one small thing that went better than you expected today?
prompts.guidance: It can be tiny — a good coffee, a reply you were dreading that landed fine.

prompts.question: Where did you spend energy that you would rather keep for tomorrow?
prompts.guidance: Naming it is enough — you are not solving it tonight.

prompts.question: What is one thing you want to carry gently into tomorrow?

zoneladder.title: Your five heart-rate zones

zones.name: Zone 1 · Recovery
zones.effort: Very easy — you could chat all day
zones.purpose: Warm-up, cool-down, and active recovery between hard days

zones.name: Zone 2 · Endurance
zones.effort: Comfortable; full sentences with light breathing
zones.purpose: Builds your aerobic base and fat metabolism — where most miles live

zones.name: Zone 3 · Tempo
zones.purpose: Sustained-effort fitness and stamina for race pace

zones.name: Zone 4 · Threshold
zones.effort: Hard; a word or two at a time
zones.purpose: Raises the pace you can hold before lactate builds up

zones.name: Zone 5 · VO₂ max
zones.effort: All-out; no talking, short intervals only
zones.purpose: Peak aerobic power — kept to brief, repeated bursts

zoneladder.caption: Zones are from an estimated max of ~195 bpm; a field or lab test gives truer numbers.

thoughtrecord.title: Working through Wednesday
thoughtrecord.situation: Looking at Wednesday’s back-to-back schedule Tuesday night.
thoughtrecord.automaticThought: If I drop one thing on Wednesday, everyone will see I can’t actually handle this job.
evidenceFor: A meeting conflict slipped through last month and I had to reschedule a client call.
The calendar really is packed, with no buffer between meetings.
evidenceAgainst: I’ve gotten through weeks this dense before without dropping anything major.
My manager called out the prep work at last sprint’s review.
Back-to-back isn’t overlapping — nothing on Wednesday needs split-second multitasking.
thoughtrecord.alternativeThought: Wednesday is genuinely packed, but packed isn’t the same as unmanageable — a few minutes of prep Tuesday night turns it into one meeting at a time.
thoughtrecord.footer: The intensity dropped once the evidence caught up with the fear — the schedule didn’t change, the story about it did.
